minutes.summary: The Trust Fund Commission appointed Richard Howard as vice chairman and then heard testimony from Ernie Sund, a founding devisee of the American Legion Post 283 trust fund, who clarified that eligibility is limited to Legion-eligible veterans (service during conflict years) who are three-year Lunenburg residents, not any veteran. The commission voted to accept a written clarification of donor intent based on that testimony, which the chair said avoids a probate cy pres court filing for the under-$75,000, under-20-year-old fund. Other agenda items, including treasurer/finance reports and a discussion of restricting appointees who ran contested elections, were deferred to the next meeting, set for August 27, 2026.

meetings.headline: Trust Fund Commission publicly accuses town manager and select board of blocking release of funds to veterans and the poor

meetings.headline: Trust Fund board voted to notify the Attorney General of a 50-year town breach managing charitable trusts
meetings.summary: The Board of Trust Fund Commissioners (two members, John Bowen and Richard Howard) spent nearly the entire meeting on a detailed breach notice alleging the Town of Lunenburg has failed for over 50 years to properly administer, document, and distribute numerous charitable trust funds, including missing donor declarations, an entirely missing fund, and unresolved American Legion fund eligibility requirements. The board voted to send a letter and submission packet to the Attorney General's Division of Public Charities and to the Town Manager and Select Board, giving the town 30 days to act, and also voted to amend the operating policy for the American Legion funds and adopt signature-page documents to formalize the filings. Chair Bowen also raised in commission comment concerns about the town's proposed override and his own re-election filing for the board.

what_happened.line: Commission voted unanimously to send Town Meeting a warrant article funding legal costs to unfreeze two dormant veterans' trust funds and the Worthy Poor fund.
A second unanimous vote advances a bylaw letting the Select Board approve trust distributions when the commission itself cannot reach quorum.
Both articles go next to the Select Board, with the bylaw also to the Bylaw Review Committee and a copy to the Finance Committee.
Only two of the commission's members, the chair and vice-chairman, were present for the meeting and both votes.

why_it_matters: Town Meeting in May will be asked to appropriate general-fund money for legal fees on a court petition to update decades-old veterans' trust language before those funds can be used.
The quorum bylaw is a process change: if this small commission can't muster a quorum, the Select Board could step in to approve trust distributions instead.
A vacancy on the Trust Fund Commission remains open, which is part of why quorum has become a live concern.
